_about: The Models tab of the hangar page (tools/hangar.html): every render Ryan judges, by chassis. A round adds its pictures under docs/hangar/renders/<chassis>/, moves the previous 'images' to 'before' with a summary, and writes 'when' and 'note'; then the page is republished with the new files (tools/hangar_data.py prints the files map). 'classes' is the silhouette classes section, a list of blocks shown in order.

classes.title: Silhouette classes
classes.plate: What a swapped component wears at a gun mount · the rule settled 30 September

blocks.note: Hardpoints are gun mounts. A weapon, or equipment that can look like one (a shield projector, a buff coil), wears its class at the next mount in the die's order, in its own maker's metal; armour panels and vents take a die entry and no mount, since they are applied to the whole machine. Five classes: barrel, twin barrel, rack, blade (katar-style, punching forward) and dish. A machine with more hardpoints than stock guns carries bare mount pads. Shown: a Minerva barrel, a Wainwright & Sutler rack, a Kestrel dish, an Arsenal blade.

Four refits rendered with RIFTGATE_FIT: the Honey Badger with a W&S Lance on the wrist, a Heat Sink (which shows nowhere), an Arsenal Blazethrower on the left pauldron and a Kestrel Deflector's dish on the right; the Clydesdale with an Arc Projector in place of the Lance and, on its bare mounts, a Missile Rack, Soulcutter Talons and an Overcharge Coil; the Sparrowhawk with Soulcutter Talons as a wing blade and Meteor Artillery on the other tip; the Wild Boar with a Plasma Carbine and a Blazethrower on its rear quarters.

badger.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its stock is the Rivet Gun alone, on the deck's ring as its class, the gimbals bare (the Canopy and the Coolant Jacket show nowhere); the missile box and the gimbals' autoguns went with the old stock.

before.summary: Before: twelfth round, third pass, 6 October (the missile box and the gimbals' autoguns)

clydesdale.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: the stations keep their kinds and each mount its stock part in order: the Maxigun as its class on the left turret where the autoguns were, the cheek bracket's left mount the Incendiary Shells' rack, the right bare; the lance, the mortar, the howitzer and the deck rack (the Airburst Shell's) as before.

before.summary: Before: the fifteenth notes, 6 October (the second pair of autoguns and the bare cheeks)

sparrowhawk.note: Ryan, 29 October, the second notes: each tooth round a driver's inlet runs its back face aft as a strake, tapering down the drum until it meets it. The rest as the first notes left it: each Pinion Driver a ramjet-gun, a chrome drum with a lit ring tapering to a lit exhaust, the barrel out of the inlet's centre; two shots at half, one from each tip.

before.summary: Before: the first notes of 29 October (the teeth a ring round the lip)

baboon.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: every station keeps its kind, the pins renumbered to the stock's order and each part its class: the shoulders' elevating mounts carry the Halo Shield's dish (left) and the Ankle Mortar's rack (right) where the Umbra Projectors rode; the fists' outer sides the Twin Autoguns (right) and the Rivet Gun (left) where the Pulse Repeaters were; the right fist's top the Laser Carbine where the Zenith Emitter was; the left fist's top bare.

before.summary: Before: fourth round, 30 September (the Umbra Projectors, the Pulse Repeaters and the Zenith Emitter)

armadillo.note: Ryan, 29 October, the seventh notes: "Side vents are ok, but the glow needs to lean way more yellow/orange, and it needs to have a larger footprint to sell. Rear vents - same color change, and move them down and farther apart. During the vent animation, don't do the double knee bend. Lower down, open vents, close vents, come back up." Every vent glows a golden orange now (a tile of its own, amber.heat: about 255, 204, 51 at the act's height and orange on the way up, where the old ember's rim showed as 255, 123, 41); the side vents are 14 by 8 (from 10 by 6), a little down the slope, their slats thinner; the radiators sit 4.5 lower on the back panel, their centres 13.5 off the spine (from 10). The vent act sinks the shell once, opens the louvres and slides the side vents out over the flaring heat, holds, shuts them as the glow dies, and rises (the fifth, from the skirmish's angle, and the sixth, from the front, both held open; the first to fourth at rest and sealed). Hold the seal under Forms in the panel, or RIFTGATE_SEAL_DEBUG=1 in the game; RIFTGATE_ACTS_DEBUG=vent_heat loops the vent.

before.summary: Before: the sixth notes of 29 October (the radiators higher and closer on the back panel, the side vents 10 by 6, the glow the ember's red-orange)

prairie_dog.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: the projector on the rear-left corner is the stock's Halo Shield as its class, a dish facing forward; the launcher there went with the old stock. The Flakshot Repeater and the turret as before.

before.summary: Before: 9 October, sixth pass (the rear-left launcher)

dingo.note: Ryan, 29 October, the second notes: the antenna that ran up through the Translocator's cabinet is gone, the one on the other side kept. As the first notes left it: the Airburst Shell's rack on its gimbal on the roof, left of the harpoon, and the coil's rings threaded on a core; the Translocator makes its die a d5 (Ryan: "I guess that's ok").

before.summary: Before: the first notes of 29 October (an antenna through the cabinet)

goshawk.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its fourth stock piece is a Canopy, which shows nowhere, so the right wing's outer pod is empty; the deflector's dish there went with the old stock. The pods' guns and the belly mount as before.

before.summary: Before: the eighth notes, 6 October (the deflector's dish on the right outer pod)

nemesis.note: Ryan, 29 October: "give the nemesis some flare during relevant animations, like roar". Its lit visor flares white-hot in its fierce acts: blazing through the roar (the third picture, a second in), at each blow of pound_fists and each crack of crack_shoulders with the core, glaring through square_up, a flash with each meteor shot. A red light already at full red can only flare toward white, so the peaks are white and the fades pass through pink back to its resting red. RIFTGATE_ACTS_DEBUG=roar loops it.

before.summary: Before: the roar at the second notes of 29 October (the visor at its resting glow)

ammit.note: Ryan, 29 October: every Arsenal cockpit's glass lit, so the Ammit's eye strips glow red at rest and flare with the throat in its acts (they had asked for a flare that glass never gave). The rest as the stock rebuild left it: the left jaw mount the Oblation Mantle as a dish, the right bare.

before.summary: Before: the stock rebuild, 28 October (the eye strips unlit glass)

stingray.note: Ryan, 28 October: the locked Photosphere Lance on the dome turret, out of its slot; the stock in its order, each part its class: the Laser Carbine under the nose where the lance lay, the Halo Shield's dish on the right forewing, the Twin Autoguns and the Ankle Mortar at the wing tips, the left forewing's mount bare (the Coolant Jacket shows nowhere). The Zenith Emitter, the Pulse Repeater, the flare pods and the lattice dish went with the old stock. The third picture is from straight behind.

before.summary: Before: the eighth notes, 6 October (the lance under the nose and the old stock's emitters and pods)

images.alt: Earlier: stingray, from behind and above

puffin.when: The swap, the amplify lit for real, 28 October.
puffin.note: Ryan's swap (26 October: the Storm Petrel's first cut, a speedboat with a mast, reads as a research boat, which is the Puffin): the long chined boat at the light size, the skirt bow to stern, the hull thicker amidships with its bottom rising to the prow and the stern (his notes of the 27th), the Ionizer's dish down on its mast's yoke, the side plates hinged low at the chine and level under way as repulsors (their undersides carrying the lit discs), folding up in a fight as shield amplifiers (the last picture, the amplify act), one booster drawn in over the afterdeck. Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October): the plates fold nearer plumb, and the amplify lights a rim round each plate's edge with the strips, the bosses, the discs underneath and the nozzles, hot. His second notes (no glow seen; the forward disc stuck out of the plate's edge; the discs should glow): the amplify's lights had been named by a prefix the rig never matches, so nothing lit; named whole now, the rims, the strips, the bosses, the discs and the nozzles all blaze (the last picture), the build refuses a glow that labels no part, and the forward disc sits inside the plate's outline.

images.alt: puffin, the plates folded up to amplify

before.summary: Before: the eighth pass, 5 October (the wide low hull on two giant boosters, the base the Storm Petrel took).

images.alt: puffin, before, from behind and above

funnel_web.note: Ryan's go, 28 October: since the stock pass its fourth stock piece is a Canopy, which shows nowhere, so the right pod's mount is bare; the deflector's dish there went with the old stock. The model is otherwise the good-to-go of 20 October.

before.summary: Before: fourth cut, 19 October; revised on Ryan's fifth to eleventh notes, 19 and 20 October, and good to go on the eleventh (the deflector's dish on the right pod)

skua.when: Second round, the jaeger; its run a flown circle, 28 October.
skua.note: Ryan's pick from five rounds of looks (23 to 27 October, docs/looks/kestrel_skua*.png): the jaeger, the seabird's wings as the swing. A short deep fuselage into one booster, a jet's straight nose with the bird's dark cap (his last note: the bent tip at the nose ditched), the fixed arms flat from low on the flank to a wrist drum and the long hands swinging from it, the white flash across their roots, a V tail, two streamers, the fin carried back over the booster and tall, the Flechette Pod twin pods on the spine. The last picture is the strafing run, the hands swept. Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October: the strafing run and the sweep-dash read the same; it wants the Kite's treatment, bigger animations): five acts like the Kite's, the strafing run rolling in and diving hard with the pods firing at the bottom, the Kite's barrel roll with the hands swept, the stoops wider and rolled far over, the Kite's loop on the map only, and the flare nose-high with the hands rocking. The last picture is the strafing run's dive. His second notes the same day (the run "just kind of wiggles"; the wings stay extended for a barrel roll): the strafing run now climbs back and up off its hex, wings over with the hands sweeping back, dives steeply on its foe with the pods firing twice at the bottom, and climbs away rolled over with the hands spreading to brake; the barrel roll flies with the hands spread. The last picture is the run's bottom. His third notes, from the phone (the run read as bobbing and swaying, never leaving its hex; the five acts and the wings-out roll confirmed): the run and the stoops at the Kite's loop's scale, the run climbing a hex back and high, diving through its hex a full hex on and arcing back over the top, the stoops a hex wide each way. His fourth (the keyed run and stoops janky, sudden changes of direction, a reverse back to the start): both flown as paths, on the map only like the Kite's circle and eight: the run one banked circle beside its hex, climbing, diving on the far side with the pods firing, sinking back onto its hex; the stoops a figure eight over its hex, each lobe lifting and stooping at its far end. The last picture is the dive's bottom. His fifth (less jerky, no flicks): the height runs on a spline, the nose turns no faster than fifty-five degrees a second, and the hands sweep over a fifth of the way round.

before.summary: Before: the first cut, 23 October (the conventional swing-wing jet, Ryan: an F-14 poly for poly).

images.alt: skua, before, the strafing run, wings swept

needletail.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Needletail is a needle of a fuselage on a short straight stub wing with a big booster nacelle on each tip, standing upright at rest so it hovers on them, exhausts down, where the Buzzard's nacelles tilt on the shoulders of a broad-winged airframe; a long thin tail ending in a dark needle with an X of small fins; a wide spotter's canopy; the Fovea Designator a sensor ball on a mast behind it, turning and nodding, its lens lit as it paints. Its acts: the transition to level flight and back, a sidestep, designating, backpedalling on its nacelles tipped back. On the move its nacelles tilt level as it gathers speed and come upright as it slows. Ryan's to judge running.

storm_petrel.when: The swap, the field lit, the arch sleeved, 28 October.
storm_petrel.note: Ryan's swap: the Puffin's wide hull with the two giant boosters, at the medium size, for the shield off-tank; his notes of the 27th ("great"): the nose snubbed so the port doubled, the louvred vent housings back on the booster covers and vents on the prow's top and flanks. No plate: the Riot Field is the four emitter pylons on the cheeks, the lit rails along their creases and the arch over the canopy; St. Elmo's fire is the open port in the nose, a chine-shaped mouth with the corona inside (the last picture, the st_elmo act). Ryan's notes on the landing (28 October: more lit areas, much brighter when lit; the corona a white block whose act showed nothing; more livery): lit strips along the flanks and caps on the fin tips join the rails, the emitters and the arch, all far hotter when the field is up; St. Elmo's fire is a small core deep in the mouth with eight sparks round the lip and a ring inside it, dim at rest, that crackle white one after another as the hull heaves and shudders; a cobalt chine stripe, a prow panel, booster bands and the emitter pylons in the livery. His second notes: the emitter pylon ahead of each tub was a livery chunk in the way of the mount, so the emitters stand clear ahead of the muzzle and behind the breech, low and in the hull's colour; the arch's glow ran along its underside, hidden, so the arch is now a thin lit line under eight sleeves of plate with the light showing between them; the booster bands lie flush as paint. His third: the sleeves longer, covering most of the band. His fourth: the sleeves about two thirds of each span, and the arch on feet that stand on the deck (it floated).

images.alt: storm_petrel, St. Elmo's fire in the port

before.summary: Before: the first cut, 23 October (the long narrow hull under two raised riot plates and a mast, the base the Puffin took).

giant_petrel.note: Claude's first cut, 23 October (Ryan: models for every chassis ready to build, their silhouettes apart from the Kestrel roster's). From above, the view the player reads, the roster is the Kite's dart on forward-swept wings with a V tail, the Buzzard's tailless plank, the Puffin's blunt hull on stubs, and the Lammergeier's two wing pairs to come. The Giant Petrel is after the Lun: a long flying-boat hull, the longest thing Kestrel builds; eight boosters in two banks of four on canards over the bow (the Immelmann Booster), pitching to blow under the wings; short cobalt wings low on the hull with float pontoons and endplates; a tall T-tail; the Spindrift Salvo's three pairs of tubes along the spine on a plinth that elevates, each back-blast lit; the Reheat Uplink's dish behind the cockpit; two turrets. Its acts: the salvo, the Immelmann, the uplink, a traverse. On the move it runs heavy and slow, nose a touch up. Ryan's to judge running.

images.alt: giant petrel, the salvo, its battery raised

lammergeier.when: First model, the flying wing, the launcher nacelles on the skin, 28 October.
lammergeier.note: The chrome chevron drawn as a hovercraft for the Giant Petrel (the third round, docs/looks/kestrel_giant.png), given to the Lammergeier airborne on Ryan's thought of 27 October ("looks good but careful on the weapon mount placement so they don't clip"): a deeper centre body with the canopy forward and the bomb bay under it on a lit seam, four booster drums across the trailing edge, the Syrinx Drone's tubes in the leading edge's roots, the Lorentz Contractor's dish on a dorsal pylon, the mounts on the wing in the bays between the drums. The last picture is the lay_mines act. 28 October: the drone tubes sit in a pod on each leading-edge root, its face raked with the edge, so the wing's skin no longer shows inside them (Ryan's note). His second notes (the pods did not work as meant): each is now a nacelle on the leading-edge root that carries the wing's full thickness forward to a blunt raked face, top and bottom, the two tubes let into the face. His third (the box was fine; the hull-coloured tube ends clipping through its raked face were the mistake): each tube's mouth follows the face's rake, a touch proud of it, in the nacelle's dark. His fourth: the tubes bored twelve deep (an end cap is no tube). His fifth (the mouths read as end caps, not inset): each mouth is a hole cut through the face plate, the bore flush in it in the lighter plate so its far wall catches the light. His sixth (the open bores showed the wing's skin again, which the caps had hidden: the skin climbs over the bore's depth): the nacelle rides on the wing's upper skin, its underside following the skin's rise from the edge, the tubes above the skin the whole way. His seventh: the bores dark, not the hull's light plate.
